children: European stocks closed a choppy session higher on Thursday, halting three sessions of losses as markets assessed the magnitude that higher sovereign yields will hamper economic activity.
The Euro STOXX 50 rose 0.3% to 6,382 and the STOXX Europe 600 added 0.4% to 649.
Yields halted their surge this week as markets trimmed their hedges against multiple rate cuts by the European Central Bank this year.
Fresh data showed that underlying producer inflation gauges in the Eurozone were relatively tame in July, as energy prices alone triggered the surge in the headline gauge to 5.8% annually.
Banks gained traction after weakness in the sector this week with Nordea, Deutsche Bank, and ING adding over 1.5%.
Auto producers also closed higher with Volkswagen adding 4%, erasing losses from the previous session on news that it will leave the STOXX 50 index.

title: European Stocks Rebound
